content.text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents:

- A nitro group (O2N) on the upper-left carbon.
- An isocyanate group (N=C=O) on the upper-right carbon.
- A methyl group on the lower-left carbon.

Going around the ring, the lower-left carbon bearing the methyl is adjacent to the nitro-bearing carbon. The isocyanate-bearing carbon is the next one over from the nitro-bearing carbon, so it is meta to the nitro group. It is para to the methyl group, because the methyl carbon, the lower-right CH, the isocyanate carbon and the upper-left CH are positioned so that the methyl and isocyanate sit opposite each other.

Ring atoms, labelled by position:
- C1: upper-left, bearing NO2
- C2: top, CH
- C3: upper-right, bearing NCO
- C4: lower-right, CH
- C5: bottom, CH
- C6: lower-left, bearing CH3

The methyl at C6 is adjacent to C1 (nitro). C3 (NCO) is para to C6, since C3 and C6 are three bonds apart. This gives 4-methyl-3-nitrophenyl isocyanate.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(N=C=O)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]
